To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the evidence suggests that short courses of palliative radiotherapy (1 or 2 fractions) are as effective as longer schedules in terms of local control and symptom palliation.
palliative radiotherapy is a highly effective treatment for non‐small‐cell carcinoma of the lung.
the evidence supports the use of short‐course palliative radiotherapy regimens, and that selected patients with good performance may be considered for longer‐term radiotherapy schedules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of radiotherapy on the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
the use of radiotherapy in the palliation of non‐small‐cell cancer.
the use of radiotherapy in palliating the symptoms of patients with non‐small‐cell cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

palliative radiotherapy for non-small-cell lung cancer is effective in controlling pain and other troublesome local symptoms and that there is a modest survival advantage for selected patients with good performance.
there is no clear evidence to support the use of any particular dose/fractionation schedule.
a short hypofractionated schedule is appropriate for the majority of patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
palliative radiotherapy to the primary site is effective in controlling local symptoms.
palliative thoracic radiotherapy is effective and safe in controlling symptoms and may improve survival in patients with good prognostic factors.
there is a need for a randomized controlled trial to compare the efficacy of different radiotherapy regimens for palliation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to improve the quality of evidence for palliative radiotherapy for non‐small‐cell cancer.
there is no clear evidence to support the routine use of higher doses of palliative radiotherapy in the management of patients with NSCLC.
palliative radiotherapy is an effective and safe treatment modality for patients with non-small cell lung cancer.
